/guides/vanguard-der-anfang#map:area-voi: Vanguard. Named region on an original diagram; spacing and angles are not geographical. Use salvage for armour/equipment; keep Hearts and Essence separate.
/guides/vanguard-der-anfang#map:pap: Pack-a-Punch is already in Stalingrad’s starting hub. Its upgrade tiers cost 7,500, 15,000 and 30,000 Essence. Ammo-mod effects come through Covenants rather than a Pack-a-Punch ammo-mod menu. These are Vanguard’s source-documented prices, not Cold War’s price schedule. Region-level overlay only: consult the guide…
/guides/vanguard-der-anfang#map:covenant: Use Sacrificial Hearts at the Altar of Covenants for available combat effects or at the Tome of Rituals to strengthen your artifact. Covenants refresh after objectives and become stronger at later rarity; inspect the actual offers. Brain Rot supplies temporary allies, melee bonuses help close fighting, and…
/guides/vanguard-der-anfang#map:crafting: Collect the single green salvage type and use the crafting table for armour, equipment and support. Repair armour before another portal or Void session. A Heart, salvage and Essence are different resources; buying a Covenant does not upgrade your weapon. Region-level overlay only: consult the guide photographs for…
/guides/vanguard-der-anfang#map:office-p: Use the Void portal inside Von List’s Office. Survive three full rounds in its Shi No Numa area. This opens the return portal near Flinger Gate; you may stay for further survival, but take the return portal for the narrative route. Region-level overlay only: consult the guide photographs for the exact object and…
/guides/vanguard-der-anfang#map:rune: Complete the remaining portal objectives needed to open Apartments. On its top floor, find the room with a floor ritual and interact with the rune stone. Wait for the conversation and Krafft’s cue about Command Post. Region-level overlay only: consult the guide photographs for the exact object and current match…
/guides/vanguard-der-anfang#map:krafft: Go back up Command Post’s stairs and interact with the white door bearing the magical symbol. Let Krafft and the Dark Aether entities finish their conversation. Region-level overlay only: consult the guide photographs for the exact object and current match conditions.
/guides/vanguard-shi-no-numa#map:area-ma: Vanguard. Named region on an original diagram; spacing and angles are not geographical. Bait Zaballa’s mines onto the Excavation Tesla coil; take tube 3.
/guides/vanguard-shi-no-numa#map:area-fl: Vanguard. Named region on an original diagram; spacing and angles are not geographical. Collect Dormitory, Doctor’s Quarters and Dig Site wheel parts; install them.
/guides/vanguard-shi-no-numa#map:area-fi: Vanguard. Named region on an original diagram; spacing and angles are not geographical. Open the required huts, Doctor’s Quarters and Dig Site.

Take the white side door and stairs from the gaming floor down to the parking level, go through the grey door by the yellow RESTRICTED AREA sign, and use the key on the mesh door in the caged room.
/dmz/stash#key-hazard-storehouse: A key door at the Haneul Nuclear Reactor: a white corrugated storage shed marked STORAGE, with a light-blue door and blue barrels beside it, on the south shore of the reactor island.
/dmz/stash#key-reactor-02-control-room: A Rare key for the control room inside the Reactor 02 building at the Haneul Nuclear Reactor.
/dmz/stash#key-reactor-drc-locker: An Ultra key for a DRC weapons locker in the irradiated pool of Reactor 02 at the Haneul Nuclear Reactor. DMZ Codex lists it as a community-reported reward for Operation Fallen Ember.
/dmz/stash#key-the-chemists-secure-armor: A Legendary key linked to Lieutenant The Chemist. Its card says it opens a secured bunker near the boat house at the Haneul Nuclear Reactor.
/dmz/stash#key-mirae-electrical-room: A Rare key awarded for Operation Critical Extraction. It opens an electrical room on level B2 of the north-west basement car park under Mirae General Hospital. The door is a grey double door in the purple-painted section beneath a 'Danger' sign.
/dmz/stash#key-the-doctors-command-offic: A Legendary key dropped by The Doctor. It opens a converted conference room behind wooden doors in the upper-floor offices of Mirae General Hospital. An LT CRATE inside holds the Tempered Armor Vest 3D Printer recipe plus weapons and gear.
/dmz/stash#key-coin-mining-den: A Rare key given for Operation Shopping Hacks. It opens an office in a multi-storey building in NuriGO West: climb the red-railed stairwell to the landing with a large '3' painted on the wall and find the plain grey door under an OFFICE sign, beside a red fire alarm.
/dmz/stash#key-jang-uis-converted-power-: Lieutenant Jang-ui's loot room. Detonated places it in an enclosed generator room on the bottom floor of NuriGO Mall, next to the robot-dog agility course.
/dmz/stash#key-nurigo-mall-sealed-room: In an official field report, a sealed door in the underground mall beneath NuriGO Mall held a Plate Carrier recipe, rare components and a Weapon Manual, guarded by robot dogs.
/dmz/stash#key-shopping-drc-locker: An Ultra key reported to open a DRC locker in the DRC Labs under NuriGO Mall, inside the secured lower car park.
/dmz/stash#key-iskras-control-room: A Legendary key for Lieutenant Iskra's loot room. It opens a control or server room on the top floor of the broadcast building at Cheonwang Peak Array.
/dmz/stash#key-executive-arms-auction: An Epic key for an arms-auction room near the top of DBN Headquarters in The Grid. Look for a dark teal door on a carpeted office floor.
/dmz/stash#key-gas-station-electrical-ro: A Rare key for an electrical room in the gas station at the Construction Zone in The Grid. The lock is on a grey metal door beside a cork noticeboard on a brick wall with a blue stripe.
/dmz/stash#key-nenshin-it-room: An Epic key for a high-security server room on the upper floors of the Nenshin Tech Complex in The Grid. One was found as random loot in a residential locker.
/dmz/stash#key-rozes-high-rise-armory: A Legendary key tied to Lieutenant Roze. It opens an armory in the upstairs offices of the Nenshin Tech Complex in The Grid, behind a teal door in a teal-walled corridor. One guide found the key in Roze's cache at DBN Headquarters.
/dmz/stash#key-old-barber-shop: A named key room in Songdo Wharf, reached through a shop and a checkerboard-tiled corridor. The pale door next to a wall phone and noticeboard reads OLD BARBER SHOP.
/dmz/stash#key-police-weapon-depository: An Epic key for an auxiliary police armory just north of the police station at Wolves Stadium. It is a different key from the Police Station Armory key.
/dmz/stash#key-shop-records-room: A Rare key for a records room in a shop building at Wolves Stadium. Enter through the grey-framed glass double doors in the red-brick wall, cross the shop floor and find the frosted-glass door in a narrow hallway next to an apartment-sale poster.
/dmz/stash#key-militia-arms-depot-key: A key for the Militia Arms Depot; a launch-day video shows where to find it.
/dmz/stash#key-black-market-weapons-lock: Key included in the Recon Equipment Kit awarded at DMZ Level 46.
/dmz/stash#key-police-station-armory: Police Stations contain a locked Armory. Infinity Ward mentions a hole in one police station armory that leads through an underwater passage.
/dmz/stash#key-bank-branch-vault-access: A Rare key that DMZ Codex says opens currency storage rooms in South Korean bank branches. No exact bank or room is recorded yet.
/dmz/stash#key-black-keycard: A keycard listed in CODMunity's item database with no further details.
/dmz/stash#key-goranis-scout-overlook-ke: A locked key room at the Goranis Scout Overlook, shown in a launch-day video.
/dmz/stash#key-hoesik-supply-room-key: Opens the Hoesik supply room; a launch-day guide video shows the door it fits.
/dmz/stash#key-lucera-suite-703-bedroom-: Opens the bedroom of Lucera Suite 703; a guide video shows the room and its loot.
/dmz/stash#key-police-station-key: Key included in the Recon Equipment Kit awarded at DMZ Level 19.
/dmz/stash#key-silo-control-room: An unmarked underground bunker in western Hajin holds two locked rooms. Its entrance needs no code; at the end of the main hallway a locked bunker room needs a key that spawns at random in the side rooms, and a separate SILO CONTROL ROOM past silo 42 is also locked.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-deployment: Each deployment starts by choosing Story Missions (replayable narrative missions), Dynamic Operations (drop straight into a generated Op for cash and XP) or Free Roam (no mission, open exploration of Hajin City and surroundings).
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-ready-up-m: The last screen before deploying, where you can take the Free Loadout, edit your Loadout and Backpack, swap Active Duty Operator, toggle Squad Fill or cancel.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-squads-squ: You can deploy solo or with a squad. With Squad Fill on, matchmaking puts you in with two other players, which is recommended if you have no group.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-free-loado: A basic gear set you can equip at Ready Up to jump in fast without spending cash or printing; if you extract, you keep those items.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-health-and: Operators spawn with 150 health, which regenerates slowly. If downed with no Self-Revive, every Operator gets one Tourniquet that brings you back up in a wounded state, after which you need a Medkit or Bandage to recover fully.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-wounds-and: Taking a Wound lowers your effective health until treated. Bandages temporarily restore max health, while a Medkit fully repairs wounds and lets you use the tourniquet to stand up from Last Stand.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-death-and-: If you die and are not revived, or fail to exfil, everything in your Backpack outside Secure Slots is lost and the Operator goes MIA. DMZ XP earned during the deployment still counts, and any Bounty on you is cleared.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-loadout-sl: The DMZ Loadout has dedicated slots for cash, armor, Dog Tag, headgear, Self-Revive, two weapons, Plate Carrier, Tactical, Lethal, Backpack, Field Upgrade, Fire Support, Mission Item, Parachute and Melee.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-stealth-me: When AI start to spot you, an audio cue plays and a HUD indicator shifts from white to yellow to orange. Dropping prone or breaking line of sight freezes and calms the meter, which helps solo players choose their fights.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-hostiles-k: A HUD meter tracks how many AI you have killed in the current deployment. When it fills, an enemy Hunt Squad is sent after you and you become Marked for Death.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-escalating: The threat system watches your activity and sends stronger reinforcements as you draw attention, such as attack helicopters, heavier troops and eventually Deathstalkers. Infinity Ward says enemy vehicles can now chase you on roads and Tier 3 troops arrive by helicopter or ground vehicle.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-dmz-hud: The DMZ HUD differs from Multiplayer: it shows a Tac-Map, a storm timer, mission objectives on the left and DMZ Orders on the right, a 1-360 compass with the current POI name, the area Threat Level, a hostile kill meter and detailed squad status.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-truces-and: Besides Proximity Chat, the Ping Wheel gives silent commands, including requesting a Truce with another squad or asking to assimilate with them.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-proximity-: You can hear (or mute) nearby rival Operators. Voice now fades with distance, is directional, and picks up reverb from the surrounding space.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-after-acti: Shown after every deployment, success or not, in four parts: Report (loot and cash banked), Rating (F to S++ from Objectives, Combat and Looting), Level (DMZ XP and Dog Tag progress) and Summary (Orders completed and rewards).
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-bounties-a: Killing other players gives you a Bounty that grows over multiple deployments; after four player kills you become Wanted, with further Wanted tiers up to Most Wanted. Nearby Operators are alerted when a Wanted player is close.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-bounty-hun: At a Bounty Station in Hajin you can see Wanted players in your match for free and pay DMZ Cash for intel that marks a search circle on your Tac-Map. You must kill the target and extract with their Dog Tag to be paid.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-movement-i: DMZ uses Modern Warfare 4's full movement set, including climbing pipes and fluid traversal of obstacles.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-dynamic-we: Hajin has changing weather: downpours cut visibility and fog banks or overcast skies make familiar routes harder to read.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-lobby-size: Matches hold up to 60 players as 20 squads of three.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-match-leng: Hands-on reports describe a roughly 30-minute radiation clock per run, with no late joins reported by PC Gamer.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-persistent: Everything you extract is persistent, unlike the 2022 DMZ which only kept cash and one backpack. Reveal-era summaries say no hard wipes are planned.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-threat-lev: Each POI has a threat level from Low to Extreme shown under the compass. Noise and fighting raise it, stealth and leaving lower it, and higher threat means better loot. It counts AI only.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-radiation-: A radiation storm spreads and intensifies across Hajin during a deployment, with a Time Remaining counter showing when it will worsen. It is the cue to head for an exfil.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-irradiated: The Haneul reactor is the main irradiated area, strongest inside the reactor building, and needs both Radiation Gear and a Gas Mask. Radiation Blockers can be printed to help in irradiated spots.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-reconnect-: If a player disconnects, they can rejoin the same deployment as long as that server is still running.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-tactical-s: Tac Sprint is on by default. It uses up stamina and then drops to normal sprint; Energy Drinks, Stims and Smelling Salts refill or extend stamina. A setting lets you control Tac Sprint manually.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-kill-feed-: The DMZ kill feed shows eliminations but not downs. Dead operators get a new world marker, said to be shown as vultures.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-few-player: In early matches some players met few or no enemy squads, but every area was full of AI. Radiation spreads across the map late in a match.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-inventory-: You equip, drop or stow items with a single button. With a full backpack, you press the backpack button to choose what to swap out, and the loot screen never fully blocks your view. In the stash, Sort is a working button and Merge Stacks is under Stash Options.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-missing-at: According to a community recap of the developer AMA, there is no night mode at launch and no in-game looking-for-group or party finder.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-ai-do-not-: GamesBeat reports, relaying co-director Joe Cecot, that North Korean AI will not attack you inside hospitals, which makes them a refuge; other players can still follow you in for the healing loot.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-generator-: Many locked areas in big POIs have no power. Find the generator, often in a basement or garage, and start it (it has skill checks) to bring doors and systems back. In the casino, the yellow portable generator on the parking level must run before the vault cameras work.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-security-c: Most major POIs seem to have a security room where you can cycle through cameras and act through them, such as opening locked gates or spotting clues for other puzzles. At the casino, the CCTV desk in penthouse security has a Parking Levels station whose camera opens the vault fence.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-k9-battery: Some locked doors are wired to a broken, sparking fuse box. Nearby crates release kamikaze robot dogs; shoot one and grab its dropped battery before it blows up, because a destroyed battery is useless. Enough batteries in the box opens the door. Operation Shopping Hacks uses this for a lab door that needs four…
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-keypad-doo: Besides named keys, some POI doors and cells use four-digit keypads. Players have found notes with partial codes, for example in the Citadel South Wing, but had not confirmed where full codes spawn. Mission keypads use your own run's digits from a laptop, keycode parts or a marked safe.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-pvp-time-t: Many players find DMZ's time-to-kill very short, shorter than the old DMZ, with one testing about one armor plate per assault-rifle body shot at range. Critics say it rewards whoever shoots first and makes disengaging hard.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-ai-ammo-dr: Players say killed AI drop little or no ammo, so it's easy to run dry on missions and end up using a bot's gun with a single magazine.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-footstep-a: Players report AI make no footstep sound, and rival players' steps vanish in noisy fights or are barely audible when they crouch-walk.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-no-plea-sy: There's no way to plead for help or to revive an enemy player, so a downed operator is usually finished off. If you're downed with no way to get up, a 'Hold to give up' prompt ends your run.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-no-map-whi: Once you are knocked down you can't open the map.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-squadmates: The game doesn't tell you when squadmates quit the match, so a solo player can run to revive teammates who have already left.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-paid-infil: For Dynamic Operations and Free Roam you choose how to enter Hajin; better options cost DMZ Cash and some need progression. Only the Cargo Plane lets you pick an exact drop point.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-exfil-site: Exfil points are drawn from a pool of locations each match and marked with green smoke. Call the helicopter, hold the site while enemy pressure rises, then board to finish the deployment; rival squads often ambush exfils.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-alternate-: Besides helicopter exfil sites you can leave by Fulton balloon or by flare. Flares are very loud and visible from far away; the June post also mentions skyhooks.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-successful: Extracting keeps your Loadout and Backpack, banks your cash, permanently unlocks any Recipes and Weapon Manuals, and applies Dog Tag level-ups and Trait Points.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-flare-exfi: Lets you call an exfil helicopter from anywhere, at the cost of attracting enemies. Crafted beforehand or found.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-fulton-bal: Fastest way out: a balloon line picked up by a passing plane. Crafted or found; hands-on mentions a roof Skyhook.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-story-miss: Some story missions have their own exfil step. Silent Ledger ends with extracting the printing plates by helicopter, and Iron Citadel sends a helicopter near the base fence after the SAM site is captured. Grid Assault and Fallen Ember only show MISSION COMPLETE, so you need a normal exfil.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-exfil-camp: Players widely report squads lying in wait at exfil sites to ambush teams who call the chopper, and many expect it to get worse. Some wait for another squad to leave first, others stick to exfils outside the city, and players are asking for quieter or paid extraction options.
/dmz/hajin?pin=14th-political-prison#int: Hajin sits where Russia and the Korean peninsula meet and is one of the largest Call of Duty environments built. It has 13 major POIs and over 60 named locations on former North and South Korean ground, with secret areas, water-only entrances and environmental storytelling.

A huge walled prison on a cleared plateau in the North Korean wilderness, with corner watchtowers, a south gate checkpoint, barracks to the east, construction on the east side and a polluted river to the west. Its Y-shaped inner Citadel is a maze of walkways, cell blocks and a furnace.
/dmz/hajin?pin=chang-san-air-base#intel-: A heavily guarded air base cut into a granite hillside, with a hospital, helipad, runway, barracks, depots and a command building. Its underground bunker and tunnel network is larger than the surface base; recon teams have got in from the wooded high ground to the south.
/dmz/hajin?pin=deadtown#intel-deadtown: An abandoned farming town taken over by the military, between toxic rivers, with sewers under the key buildings and two Re-Education Centers at its heart. It has a Clinic, a Gas Station at each end, and fake residential blocks hiding military storage on the east side.
/dmz/hajin?pin=imjin-farmland#intel-imji: An open floodplain of rice fields, waterways and rail lines on the old border, dominated by a large Rice Mill with warehouses. Long sightlines and little cover favor vehicles and careful movement; grid D7 on the Tac-Map.
/dmz/hajin?pin=cheongun-village#intel-ch: The most northerly former-SK area, a riverside village split by border posts toward Russia, with Expressway No. 1 to the south. The multi-floor Heavenly Luck Casino with underground parking dominates it; the fog-covered Russian side of the river is off limits.
/dmz/hajin?pin=mirae-general-hospital#in: Hajin's main hospital, next to a train station and near The Grid and the mall, with triage tents and temporary barracks outside and color-coded wards inside. Snipers may watch from the wooded array area at Mujin Pass to the south.
/dmz/hajin?pin=cheonwang-peak-array#inte: Hajin's largest telecom array, the DBN TV station on a summit in the South Korean wilderness, now an enemy barracks. Boulder trails lie to the west and the roof has a helipad with long views.
/dmz/hajin?pin=haneul-nuclear-reactor#in: A breached nuclear plant under a lingering radioactive cloud; entry requires protective gear and a gas mask. The breach centers on the containment block across Reactor 02 while Reactor 01 holds; access by water or a tunnel from Compound Delta is possible.
/dmz/hajin?pin=nurigo-mall#intel-nurigo-: A shopping district with a police station, clinic, City Hall, Han-Go Korean BBQ and a monorail station. A courtyard with a pavilion and two light wells (one with an elevator) leads down to a large dark underground mall where NVGs help.
/dmz/hajin?pin=the-grid#intel-the-grid: A fortified business district behind a steel and razor-wire wall, from Donpyeong Gate past Hanex Bank, the DBN TV tower (Hajin's tallest building) and the red-roofed twin towers of the tech complex to Minsok Art School and a big construction zone. Expect rooftop and street-level fighting with few escape routes; Hotel…
/dmz/hajin?pin=songdo-wharf#intel-songdo: A coastal district between the reactor and the river's south fork with working train and monorail lines and signs of an amphibious landing. It includes the La Grande Vie tower, a tent market, a pier and lighthouse, a park and the Oamsik Turtle Island rock outcrop.
/dmz/hajin?pin=wolves-stadium#intel-wolv: The ruined home ground of the Wolves baseball team, with Baseball Stadium B Station, a deserted open-air Theatre to the north and nearby Police Station and bank. The northern edge bordering The Grid is the most dangerous part.
/dmz/hajin?pin=hajin-river-heights#intel: A battered residential district rising toward the river's south fork and a long green bridge. One apartment block is now Compound Echo; Jinseo Park Towers and a comms tower on South Island lie further south.
/dmz/hajin?pin=songdo-wharf#intel-hajin-: Hajin's main river rises in the western mountains and splits into north and south branches before reaching the sea near the reactor and Songdo Wharf.
/dmz/hajin?pin=tong-il-village#intel-ton: A farming village on the river's northern delta floodplain, marked by a large statue of a former leader.
/dmz/hajin?pin=revolution-dam#intel-revo: An intact dam guarded by a strong military police presence, northwest of Tong-il Village.
/dmz/hajin?pin=pyonghwa-village#intel-py: Homes and farmland west of the river with a damaged pontoon bridge that lets vehicles cross quickly.
/dmz/hajin?pin=imjin-suburb#intel-imjin-: A small riverside hamlet for farm workers at the base of a wooded hill near the railway.
/dmz/hajin?pin=mujin-pass#intel-mujin-pa: A farming community in a dell on a main road between two forests, with the Hospital to the north and the Array to the south.
/dmz/hajin?pin=daesong-ridge#intel-daeso: A rural settlement northeast of Imjin Farmland where burned-out APCs line a cratered road.
/dmz/hajin?pin=namjin-riverside#intel-na: Southern-edge area by the river's south fork with abandoned civilian cars near a tunnel exit.
/dmz/hajin?pin=hanrim-village#intel-othe: The official Tac Map adds secondary labels not described in the blogs, including Jayon Warehouses, Hanrim Village and three Russian Border Crossings.
/dmz/hajin?pin=14th-political-prison#int: The Y-shaped inner fortress of the 14th Political Prison, full of gantries, cell blocks, repatriation chambers, a furnace and high-value targets; easy to get cut off in.
/dmz/hajin?pin=cheongun-village#intel-he: A once-luxurious multi-floor casino with underground parking and dark gambling halls; NVGs recommended, and it holds a vault.
/dmz/hajin?pin=chang-san-air-base#intel-: A North Korean administrative building with a large statue, marked as a fortress on the official Tac Map next to the Chang-san Air Base label.
/dmz/hajin?pin=deadtown#intel-re-educati: One of Deadtown's two central re-education buildings where enemy numbers build up; marked as a fortress on the Tac Map.
/dmz/hajin?pin=imjin-farmland#intel-rice: A large industrial mill with warehouses that overlooks the surrounding farmland; marked as a fortress on the Tac Map.
/dmz/hajin#intel-compounds: Small and medium fortified military sites that are heavily defended and hold better loot and intel. Going in loud brings more defenders, and armored vehicles like the LTV can be found there; the Tac Map marks six (Alpha to Foxtrot).
/dmz/hajin?pin=compound-alpha#intel-comp: A fortified enemy compound marked on the official Tac Map.
/dmz/hajin?pin=compound-bravo#intel-comp: A fortified enemy compound marked on the official Tac Map.
/dmz/hajin?pin=compound-charlie#intel-co: A fortified enemy compound marked on the official Tac Map.
/dmz/hajin?pin=compound-delta#intel-comp: A fortified enemy compound marked on the official Tac Map. A tunnel leads from Compound Delta toward the Haneul Nuclear Reactor.
/dmz/hajin?pin=compound-echo#intel-compo: A fortified enemy compound marked on the official Tac Map. Compound Echo is an apartment building in Hajin River Heights turned into a military base.
/dmz/hajin?pin=compound-foxtrot#intel-co: A fortified enemy compound marked on the official Tac Map.
/dmz/hajin#intel-gas-stations: Found across Hajin; they repair and refuel ground and air vehicles and refill Gas Cans. The Tac Map marks 18.
/dmz/hajin#intel-marine-gas-stations: Small jetties with two pumps that repair and refuel boats (and nearby vehicles) and refill Gas Cans. The Tac Map marks 6.
/dmz/hajin#intel-fire-stations: Red buildings, brick in former NK areas and modern in SK areas, usually guarded; good for Radiation Gear and Parachutes. The Tac Map marks 6.
/dmz/hajin?pin=cheongun-village#intel-po: Blue buildings with many rooms, sometimes roof access, military gear and a locked Armory. The Tac Map marks 5.
/dmz/hajin#intel-clinics-and-hospitals: Green-fronted local clinics that may hold medical loot; watch for players camping them. The Tac Map has 8 clinic markers (two share the same spot).
/dmz/hajin#intel-ammo-and-armor-caches: Caches, often inside enemy compounds, that refill ammo and give Armor Plates, then go on cooldown. The Tac Map marks 28.
/dmz/hajin#intel-bounty-stations: Rugged laptops in Hajin for viewing bounties on players in your match, buying intel on them, or paying off your own bounty with DMZ Cash.
/dmz/hajin?pin=cheongun-village#intel-dy: Phones placed in Hajin that let you start a Dynamic Operation mid-deployment.
/dmz/hajin?pin=haneul-nuclear-reactor#in: The irradiated area around the reactor in the northeast is where the meltdown happened. You need a gas mask or hazmat gear, and it holds loot found nowhere else.
/dmz/hajin#intel-official-interactive-ta: Activision published an interactive web map of Hajin on 19 Oct 2026 with POIs, fortresses, compounds, stations, caches, UAV Towers and Lieutenant Towers.
/dmz/hajin?pin=cheongun-village#intel-ex: Hajin's main freeway, running east-west south of Cheongun Village and north of the Hospital.
/dmz/hajin?pin=nurigo-mall#intel-hajin-c: The urban eastern part of the map, made up of NuriGO Mall, The Grid, Songdo Wharf and Wolves Stadium. An automated monorail tram loops through it.
/dmz/hajin#intel-residential-districts: Activision's June description says residential areas across Hajin mainly yield crafting materials and scavenged resources.
/dmz/hajin?pin=14th-political-prison#int: The walled yard of the 14th Political Prison around The Citadel. Dexerto used it as the example of a sub-area rated differently from its parent's core.
/dmz/hajin?pin=chang-san-air-base#intel-: The surface section of Chang-san Air Base, with its runway, helipad, hospital, barracks, depots and command building.
An underground complex reached through hidden tunnels and larger than the air base above it. It is one of only two Extreme zones in Hajin.
A depot inside the Chang-san bunker where Lieutenant Bale waits with specialised guards. CODMunity says the Dynamic Op Chemical Denial leads there.
/dmz/hajin?pin=deadtown#intel-deadtown-e: The open streets and farmland of Deadtown outside the Re-Education Center.
/dmz/hajin?pin=imjin-farmland#intel-farm: The open rice fields and waterways of Imjin Farmland.
/dmz/hajin?pin=imjin-farmland#intel-jeon: A loading dock zone inside Imjin Farmland.
/dmz/hajin?pin=cheongun-outskirts#intel-: The edges of Cheongun Village near the Russian border crossing.
/dmz/hajin?pin=russian-border-crossing#i: A border crossing zone attached to Cheongun Village on the north edge of the playable map.
/dmz/hajin?pin=russian-border-crossing-w: A second border crossing named on the official Tac-Map. DMZMap places it beyond the top edge of the map image.
/dmz/hajin?pin=russian-border-crossing-e: A border crossing named on the Tac-Map that DMZMap groups with the Haneul Nuclear Reactor.
/dmz/hajin?pin=haneul-nuclear-reactor#in: The approach zone around the reactor that you cross by water or tunnel to reach the plant.
The reactor unit with a major breach, the source of the area's heavy radiation.
The second reactor unit, described as stable for now.
/dmz/hajin?pin=nurigo-east#intel-nurigo-: The eastern half of the NuriGO shopping district; an Open Bounty Station sits on a rooftop nearby.
/dmz/hajin?pin=nurigo-west#intel-nurigo-: The more dangerous western half of the NuriGO shopping district.
/dmz/hajin?pin=nurigo-mall#intel-nurigo-: A large subterranean mall under the NuriGO courtyard with no power, so NVGs are needed. Expel reports a sealed door down here opened with a key from The Warden.
/dmz/hajin?pin=nurigo-mall#intel-city-ha: A surface building in the NuriGO district listed as a key spot.
/dmz/hajin?pin=nurigo-mall#intel-han-go-: A restaurant listed as a key spot on the NuriGO Mall surface.
/dmz/hajin?pin=the-grid#intel-nenshin-te: Twin towers inside The Grid and the only non-military Extreme zone on the map.
/dmz/hajin?pin=dbn-headquarters#intel-db: A Critical zone in The Grid. The DBN TV tower, Hajin's tallest building, is listed as The Grid's key spot.
/dmz/hajin?pin=hanex-bank#intel-hanex-ba: A bank tower inside The Grid.
/dmz/hajin?pin=the-grid#intel-minsok-art: An art school zone inside The Grid.
/dmz/hajin?pin=construction-zone#intel-c: A construction site zone listed under The Grid.
/dmz/hajin?pin=cheonwang-peak-array#inte: The broadcast array on Cheonwang Peak, now held by enemies, with barracks inside and a helipad on the roof.
/dmz/hajin?pin=songdo-wharf#intel-oamsik: A small island off Songdo Wharf.
/dmz/hajin?pin=shoreline-station#intel-s: A station zone on the Songdo waterfront that contains La Grande Vie.
/dmz/hajin?pin=songdo-pier#intel-songdo-: A pier named on the Tac-Map next to Songdo Wharf.
/dmz/hajin?pin=songdo-wharf#intel-la-gra: A building at Shoreline Station; in the story chapter Underground you place a Transmitter on its roof.
/dmz/hajin?pin=wolves-stadium#intel-thea: An abandoned open-air theatre beside Wolves Stadium.
/dmz/hajin?pin=wolves-stadium#intel-base: A transit station listed as Wolves Stadium's key spot.
/dmz/hajin?pin=south-island#intel-south-: An island zone in Hajin River Heights with a comms tower.
/dmz/hajin?pin=hajin-river-heights#intel: Residential towers next to a ceremonial park in Hajin River Heights.
/dmz/hajin?pin=hanrim-village#intel-hanr: A village in the north whose surrounding woods are the hunting ground of Lieutenant Gorani. DMZMap places it beyond the top edge of the map image.
/dmz/hajin?pin=jayon-warehouses#intel-ja: A named place on the Tac-Map that DMZMap places beyond the top edge of the map image.
/dmz/hajin#intel-the-epic: A named place on CODMunity's list of smaller Hajin locations; no description is given.
/dmz/hajin?pin=the-grid#intel-hotel-luce: A named place on CODMunity's list of smaller Hajin locations; no description is given.
/dmz/hajin#intel-fortresses: Seven heavily guarded strongholds are marked on the official Tac-Map. Both map sites list the same seven.
/dmz/hajin?pin=cheongun-village#intel-ru: Hajin borders Russia, but the Russian section is fogged and unreachable at launch and is planned as an expansion of the existing map rather than a separate map.
/dmz/hajin#intel-xl1: A new DMZ location arriving with Season 1 that Infinity Ward compares to Building 21 from the 2022 DMZ. No layout or access details are public.
/dmz/hajin?pin=imjin-farmland#intel-haji: Hajin becomes a Warzone battle royale map with Season 1. Parts of it, Imjin Farmland and Wolves Stadium, also ship as Ground War Combat Outpost maps.
/dmz/hajin?pin=imjin-farmland#intel-tac-: The in-game grid runs letters west to east and numbers north to south; Activision's example is that D7 is Imjin Farmland. Every key's description names its grid square.
/dmz/hajin#intel-community-interactive-m: Community sites published interactive Hajin maps with the official location markers before launch, including DMZHUB.GG and DMZ Codex. The r/DMZ moderators partnered with DMZHUB.GG, which also tracks loot and imports 3D Printer recipes.
/dmz/hajin#intel-campaign-mission-locati: A player mapped the MW4 campaign missions that take place in Hajin by matching campaign videos against the DMZ map, and rates it about 95% accurate.
/dmz/hajin?pin=cheongun-village#intel-ca: A flooded tunnel links the Cheongun Village police station, just west of the casino, to the Heavenly Luck Casino car park. From the station's lowest basement drop through a hole into the water, swim on, then follow a dry corridor (watch for tripwires) into the garage and up the stairs to the vault gate.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-camper: A fast but unarmored camper for moving the squad; avoid taking fire in it.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-sedan: A small civilian car, not built for combat, for quick travel.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-grizzly: A lightly armored but agile vehicle based on a Soviet design, good for hit-and-run.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-dreadnough: An Aston Martin armored all-wheel-drive tactical SUV with strong off-road ability; found at a few key POIs in DMZ and Warzone.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-polaris-da: A tough off-road tactical vehicle that carries a full squad; also available as a 5,000-cash infil drop.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-ltv: A light combat vehicle with an optional mounted .50 cal; found at Compounds and available as a 25,000-cash infil drop.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-cargo-truc: A diesel military truck with a two-seat cab and a flatbed.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-d50-radar-: A diesel military truck variant with a UAV mounted on the vehicle.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-train: An automated civilian train, not player-driven, that runs a winding route through many former-SK POIs.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-tram: A slow, automated elevated monorail carriage looping around the outskirts of Hajin City; NuriGO Mall has a station.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-armored-pa: An armored boat named in the Marine Gas Station description as benefiting from refueling there.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-heli: A twin-engine combat helicopter for fast movement and air support.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-heavy-chop: A heavily armored transport helicopter with defensive flares; it hovers on autopilot if the pilot leaves while fuel remains. Rarely player-controlled.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-monarch: A twin-rotor heavy-lift helicopter that handles infil and exfil; not player-controlled.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-fuel-and-r: Unlike Warzone, DMZ vehicles have limited fuel and armour and must be refuelled and repaired at Gas Stations or Marine Gas Stations, or topped up with Gas Cans.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-tier-1-grunts: Basic North Korean infantry. Infinity Ward says these entry-level enemies have no armor or helmet so first fights are manageable.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-tier-2-armored-sol: Armored North Korean infantry, a step above the basic grunts.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-tier-3-gas-masked-: Armored soldiers in gas masks. Infinity Ward describes them as white-masked troops with garbled voices who show up as you keep raising the threat.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-tier-4-faceless: The top regular infantry tier: faceless, armored North Korean soldiers.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-autonomous-combat-: Swarms of small autonomous attack drones; a field report shows them filling the sky over an exfil site. Hajin has four enemy drone types in total.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-autonomous-lmg-com: An autonomous drone armed with a light machine gun, one of four drone types in Hajin.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-autonomous-k9-quad: Four-legged robot dogs that are usually found underground; a field report has them hunting through the tunnels beneath NuriGO Mall.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-attack-infantry-he: Enemy helicopters patrol Hajin and join as reinforcements; Infinity Ward says soldiers ride on the sides and shoot at you.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-road-convoys: Enemy vehicle convoys travel Hajin's roads, and at higher threat enemy vehicles can chase players.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-hunt-squad: An enemy squad dispatched to track you once your Hostiles Kill Count meter fills, leaving you Marked for Death.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-commanders: Heavily armored roaming bosses that are always present somewhere in Hajin; intel on them is free and cannot be bought. They show on the Tac-Map when near and your Team Leader warns you; kills pay DMZ Cash (first kill of each), XP and prized printer ingredients if you extract.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-colossus: A seven-foot, heavily armored soldier carrying a minigun that fires depleted-uranium rounds. A field report shows one joining the enemy response at an exfil.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-deathstalker: A helicopter-sized autonomous drone with twin machine-gun turrets; one of four drone types in Hajin. Higher threat can bring Deathstalkers after you, and captured SAM Sites help against them.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-lieutenants: Battle-hardened high-value targets with unique loadouts, extra durability, distinct tactics and sometimes escorts; they may be active whether or not you hunt them. A splash screen warns you when one is near.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-bale: In an official field report, Bale is a hardened Spetsnaz veteran working with North Korean forces as a trainer and enforcer, defending Chang-san Air Base with elite troops.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-the-warden: A Lieutenant fought in the mess hall of the 14th Political Prison. In an official field report he is sniped in the northern hills and drops a key stamped for a sealed door beneath NuriGO Mall.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-the-doctor: A Lieutenant in a white hazmat suit and gas mask who holds Mirae General Hospital. He charges at close range, and his Command Office key opens an upper-floor office whose crate can hold the Tempered Armor Vest recipe.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-north-korean-force: The main AI faction is North Korean troops trying to seize chemical, biological and nuclear weapons in Hajin. They guard key areas, move in convoys and squads, and fly helicopters.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-juggernauts: Activision's June material listed Juggernauts among roaming Commander-level threats. The October field guide does not list them by that name.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-elite-strike-teams: June material listed Elite Strike Teams (Man of Many: elite hunter teams) as an escalation threat. The October field guide does not name them.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-auto-turrets: PC Gamer's reviewer met Lieutenant Jang-ui in a room with auto-turrets in all four corners that nearly killed them.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-elevator-reinforce: CODMunity's guide notes that AI reinforcements can arrive through elevators.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-main-nk-battle-tan: A North Korean main battle tank on high alert that patrols Hajin's roads.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-general-kang: A North Korean general and the high-value target of Operation Critical Extraction at Mirae General Hospital, whom you move to safety on his hospital bed. CODMunity says he is not a boss.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-jang-ui: A Lieutenant fought on the upper floor of the Nenshin Tech Complex in The Grid (Extreme), in a turret-lined server hall marked 14. Pre-launch official material put his encampment in NuriGO Mall, which launch guides now give as the site of his loot room.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-the-scavenger: From The Ward mentioned a side op called 'Kill the Scavenger' that drops a Legendary Scavenger's Dog Tag. The Fandom wiki lists the Scavenger as a Lieutenant.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-jin-tae: Jin-Tae is the Lieutenant of the Heavenly Luck Casino (HIGH) in Cheongun Village. He opens with heavy automatic fire on the casino floor, so guides advise falling back through the double doors into the staff offices and killing him as he comes down the office corridor. He drops the ISO Nightshade SMG and his dog tag.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-roze: Roze is a sniper Lieutenant at DBN Headquarters in The Grid (EXTREME). She fights from the rooftop terraces among vents and a radio mast, or from a top-floor machine room by the roof door, and one shot can down you. Climb the stairs using the rails as cover. The Deathstalker also patrols this roof.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-iskra: Iskra holds the office building at Cheonwang Peak Array (MEDIUM). Iskra fires from an upper doorway and then runs down the stairwell, so chase and finish the fight on a landing. The kill pays 1,000 XP and can drop the Widowmaker, a Legendary shotgun, or the Warlord.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-the-chemist: The Chemist waits in a warehouse beside the reactor tanks inside the Haneul Nuclear Reactor radiation zone (HIGH). The guards wear dark hazmat suits and the Chemist a yellow one, so bring a gas mask and Radiation Blockers. His dog tag drops on the body.
/dmz/boss-board#intel-ai-difficulty: Players describe the AI as numerous and relentless: groups of four or five at once, nonstop reinforcements and helicopters at places like Chang-san Air Base, and scout helicopters that shred you if shot at. A Steam thread says low-tier bots can wipe a squad.
/dmz/stash#intel-keys: Keys found in Hajin open special loot rooms, and every Key's description includes its Tac-Map grid location. Keys can be kept in the Stash between deployments.
/dmz/stash#intel-lieutenant-keys-and-loo: Lieutenants can drop a key to their own named loot room, where their signature weapon can usually be found if it did not drop from the body.
/dmz/stash#intel-heavenly-luck-casino-va: The casino in Cheongun Village has a vault that squads try to break into; Infinity Ward suggests using a cash-mule Operator to raid it.
/dmz/stash#intel-alternate-entrances-and: A door locked from the inside means another way in exists, and rural or wooded areas hide underground entrances; some POIs can only be entered from the water. Breaching consumables, including the Door Breacher Charge, open secured doors.
/dmz/stash#intel-casino-penthouse-cartel: A Reddit casino guide reports a cartel hideout in one of the penthouse hotel rooms of the Heavenly Luck Casino, holding rare loot crates.
/dmz/stash#intel-poi-power-and-security-: Many POIs lock loot behind small puzzles: generators restore power to dark areas, security-camera rooms can open doors, and some doors need K9 Battery Cores put into a fuse box, as in the prison's East Wing and the NuriGO lab.
/dmz/stash#intel-keys-keypad-doors: Some POI doors use random four-digit keypads instead of keys. Players say codes come from Dynamic Ops such as Broken Resupply, which show the code and mark the keypad, while the prison's South Wing cells use a keypad whose digits are spread across notes.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-dmz-orders: DMZ Orders come in pages of three, and a page pays out once all three are done. Page 1 is the tutorial; then you pick one of three chapters (Human Intel, Underground, Counterfeit), each two pages long and ending in a story mission. Every page so far pays $20,000 plus items or recipes.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-story-missions: Narrative missions that continue the Modern Warfare 4 story inside specific Hajin locations on a live server with other players. You can pick or replay them (or roll a random one) and earn high-value gear, DMZ Cash and milestone rewards.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-setting-and-pr: You play an off-the-books shadow CIA asset sent into the Hajin Exclusion Zone after the Campaign to secure abandoned military technology before hostile forces get it. Rogue Operators and enemy combatants roam the zone.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-breaking-new-g: An official CODUpdates post names Breaking New Ground as a DMZ mission that involves breaching a door. The post does not say whether it is a Story Mission or another mission type.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-dynamic-operat: Multi-step objectives generated each match, such as shutting down abandoned weapons programs, securing assets, rescues and assaults. Start one from the Deploy menu or a Dynamic Ops phone in Hajin; each completion pays DMZ XP and Cash plus a Supply Drop.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-hunt-operator: A Dynamic Op that pits you against a full squad of rival Operators.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-side-ops: Lower-intensity side activities that award DMZ XP, resources or intel while you explore. Completed Side Ops are counted in the After Action Report.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-truck-repair: Side Op where you find and repair trucks around Hajin that gain useful functions once fixed; Infinity Ward mentions trucks with a UAV mounted on the back.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-lost-supply-dr: Side Op to locate supply drops that went missing in Hajin.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-lieutenant-hun: Climb a tall, dangerous comms tower and use the laptop or terminal at the top to reveal the general location of the nearest active Lieutenant; this completes a Side Op. The official Tac Map marks five towers.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-uav-towers: Small portable comms towers, usually guarded, that complete a Side Op, pay DMZ Cash and send a pulse revealing nearby Operators and enemies. The official Tac Map marks 14.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-sam-sites: Fixed missile batteries you capture as a Side Op by hacking the control computer and defending it while a siren draws enemies. Once held, the battery shoots enemy aircraft, which helps against Deathstalkers, but enemies can retake it if you move too far away.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-joyride: An Underground 1/2 order seen completed in pre-launch trailer footage. It does not appear in early-access order lists.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-operation-crit: Hospital rescue: locate a high-value target, General Kang, at Mirae General Hospital, fight off resistance and get him out (hands-on mentions extracting from the roof).
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-operation-sile: Casino heist in Cheongun Village: get into the casino, breach the vault and recover stolen printing plates that bankroll the enemy.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-operation-shop: NuriGO Mall mission tied to Lieutenant Jang-ui: hack the network, reprogram a protocol and grab evidence from his encampment.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-operation-iron: Named story mission whose completion is reported to unlock the LTV vehicle infil.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-operation-grid: Story mission in The Grid, mostly inside DBN Headquarters with a side trip to Hanex Bank or Nenshin Tech Complex. Finishing it unlocks the Helicopter infil.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-dead-mans-cach: Dynamic Op in Cheongun Outskirts: find a hidden cache, open the HVT's room with a code, destroy an ammo and armor cache with a bomb from a dead drop, then kill the HVT.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-chemical-denia: Dynamic Operation that starts by investigating a power outage and, per the trailer, leads to Lieutenant Bale's Tank Depot.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-paid-intel: Side op shown in the trailer that points you at Lieutenant Bale: reach him, kill him. A +500 cash badge appears on completion.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-contracts: GamesBeat's hands-on mentions contracts that boost progression between matches, and Man of Many calls Lieutenants 'high-value contracts'. No site describes a formal contract system like the 2022 DMZ.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-daily-orders: GamesBeat says daily orders can be chased for higher rewards.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-damaged-radio-: Activision's June description listed scaling damaged radio towers as a Side Op. COD Central says climbing one reveals a nearby Lieutenant.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-toxic-intercep: A Dynamic Operation named in the official patch notes. One of its objectives is Defend the Bomb; a bug that failed the Op after that step was fixed on 21 Oct.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-dmz-intro-miss: First-time players start DMZ with a scripted tutorial alongside a dog named Rex: you head to a crashed drone to recover its black box and data, Rex is wounded in an ambush and hidden, and the run ends with your soldier captured and killed. It gives no loot, and Kotaku found no unlockable dogs in the mode yet.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-crashed-crate: Page 10 order 01 per COD Central: recover three Lost Supply Drops and finish a Loot Radio Tower side op. Some lost drops hang in trees or on buildings and must be brought down first.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-surprise-me: Page 10 order 02 per COD Central: complete five Dynamic Ops and finish a story mission through the Random Story Mission deploy, which only draws from missions you have completed and needs squad fill.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-healer-page-10: COD Central lists Page 10's third order under the title Healer, with crafting-material tasks that differ from the Page 7 Healer. Treat the title and wording as unverified until a second guide covers Page 10.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-random-story-m: A card under the story mission tree that deploys you into a random mission you have already completed. Threat ranges from Medium to Extreme, squad fill is required, and a weekly task asks for three random completions.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-operation-fall: Final story mission at the Haneul Nuclear Reactor (Extreme). Unlock Reactor 01, pull three fuel rods from the flooded pool, clean them at Reactor 02, secure the warhead, kill Commander Colossus for the boathouse key and escort the chopper by patrol boat. A normal exfil is needed afterwards.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-ghost-shipment: An HVT-to-SAM-site op: find and kill a marked soldier, take his Classified Orders, capture a SAM site and let it shoot down a helicopter, then loot the Lieutenant's cargo container. Start points and sites move between matches.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-signal-breaker: A bomb-building op: gather three bomb parts (one in a safe at Compound Alpha in one run), craft the bomb at a workbench and plant it on three radar trucks, which sat around Imjin Farmland in reported runs.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-viral-reckonin: The longest op COD Central has run: kill an HVT carrying a radio, rescue a scientist from behind a keypad door, carry him to a defended landing zone, then either take the bomb and plant it on a biological WMD or exfil early for partial credit.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-broken-resuppl: Its first step is hacking a Comms Server. COD Central's full run then had a defend, a marked bomb in a cache, a keypad code from a safe, and planting the bomb on a WMD of red barrels.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-special-delive: A bomb op against a mobile missile launcher: gather three bomb parts, craft the bomb, capture a UAV tower, reach the launch platform, plant and defend the bomb, then take cover.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-sky-heist: Starts with Locate the Intel and later sends you to a target SAM site. The middle steps vary between matches (hidden cache, safe, or rewiring power), and no guide has published the ending yet.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-domino-protoco: A chain op in which each marked target you kill drops intel that points to the next HVT; one run ended in front of a Lieutenant in a high-threat area. The full ending has not been published.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-ignition-point: A Dynamic Op seen in launch play. Its first step is Proceed to the Target Area (at North Fork Hajin River in one run); its later steps and rewards are not published yet.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-crack-safe: Safes are marked CRACK SAFE on the Tac Map. Hold interact on the red lock panel until it turns blue; no key or code is needed. Contents are mostly valuables and cash, such as Nuclear Program Files or Degraded Execution Footage worth $2,000.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-clear-the-mili: Kill every soldier at a military compound; the side op tracker shows progress as a percentage. Finishing it also completes the Clear a Compound step of the No One Left order.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-information-po: An order about Lieutenant intel and kills. Its Boss Board step sometimes fails to register; a guide shows a fix.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-arms-deal: A Gunsmith order: buy a gun and build one up with at least three attachments.
/dmz/intel/missions#intel-friendly-face: An order to request a truce with another squad through the ping wheel.
/dmz/operators#intel-active-duty-slots: You start with two Active Duty Operator slots and earn a third by leveling DMZ. Vault Edition owners start with three. A chosen Operator is locked to its slot until dismissed and cannot occupy two slots.
/dmz/operators#intel-permanent-prestige-: Each Operator Prestige grants one random Permanent Trait tied to that Operator, up to three. They persist through dismissal, slot changes and skin changes.
/dmz/operators#intel-operator-roster: Modern Warfare 4 launches with 33 Operators usable in both Multiplayer and DMZ. Four of them are unlocked through DMZ levels.
/dmz/operators#intel-reece: Reece is an Operator from the Shadow Company faction who is unlocked by reaching DMZ Player Level 4.
/dmz/operators#intel-coffey: Coffey is an Operator from the JSOF faction who is unlocked by reaching DMZ Player Level 9.
/dmz/operators#intel-simone: Simone is an Operator from the Shadow Company faction who is unlocked by reaching DMZ Player Level 15.
/dmz/operators#intel-hector: Hector is an Operator from the Valeria's Strike Cell faction who is unlocked by reaching DMZ Player Level 19.
/dmz/operators#intel-persistent-operator: Each operator keeps its own backpack, loadout, Dog Tag progress and trait build, while the Bank, Stash and printer ingredients are shared across all Active Duty operators.
/dmz/operators#intel-mia-and-recovery: A killed or stranded operator goes Missing In Action and cannot deploy until you pay DMZ Cash from the Bank to recover it at the Active Duty station. The price climbs with trait points invested; traits come back, gear does not.
/dmz/operators#intel-dismiss-operator: Instead of paying to recover, an MIA operator can be dismissed and a new recruit put in the slot, losing that operator's progress.
/dmz/operators#intel-dog-tag-levels: Each operator ranks its Dog Tag through 18 levels, Steel I to Onyx III (Steel, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Damascus, Onyx with three ranks each). Every level grants one Trait Point, and a new operator starts from Steel I.
/dmz/operators#intel-your-dog-tag: Your Dog Tag shows its tier, any bounty on you and the operators you have eliminated. Enemies can take it when they kill you, and extracting with it pays out the bounty.
/dmz/operators#intel-operator-prestige: Once an operator has all 18 Trait Points (Onyx III) it can be prestiged by handing over cash and rare gear. Traits and backpack contents are wiped, DMZ level is not, and the operator gets a random Permanent Prestige Trait.
/dmz/operators#intel-operator-choice-loc: A new player picked Ghost by accident as their first operator and could not find a way to change the operator or skin.
/dmz/operators#intel-trait-trees: Each Operator can earn up to 18 Trait Points to spend across three trees (Warfighter, Scout, Survivalist) holding 66 Traits in total, 22 per tree. Picks are permanent, so 18 points can max two trees or spread across all three.
/dmz/operators#intel-warfighter-tree: Combat-oriented tree. Blog examples include resetting tactical sprint on kills, recharging equipment, explosive/tactical resistance, hiding from thermals and AI targeting, faster regen on kills, a once-per-match self revive, and extra enemy drops.
/dmz/operators#intel-scout-tree: Looting and recon tree. Examples include more cash on extract, enemies dropping printer ingredients, extra container loot, UAV concealment and upgrades, permanent UAV towers, and crafting in the field.
/dmz/operators#intel-survivalist-tree: Survival and support tree. Examples include longer UAV tower and SAM site duration, faster revives, longer consumables, smoke when downed, auto-repair of the first Wound, revive buffs and an auto-exfil call while in Last Stand.
/dmz/operators#intel-vehicle-traits: Some Traits improve vehicle handling, such as getting out and fixing a punctured tire. The blog does not name these Traits.
/dmz/operators#intel-adrenaline-burst: Killing an enemy resets Tactical Sprint.
/dmz/operators#intel-equipment-professio: Equipped lethal and tactical equipment slowly recharges after use.
/dmz/operators#intel-combat-resistance: Reduces explosive damage and the effects of enemy tactical equipment.
/dmz/operators#intel-viper-sense: Hides the operator from thermal optics and AI targeting systems.
/dmz/operators#intel-quick-fix: Shortens the delay before health regeneration after killing an operator or hostile.
/dmz/operators#intel-possum: Once per match, lets you self-revive into Last Stand after being killed, with health restored to full.
/dmz/operators#intel-lt-hunter: Grants more intel from Lieutenant Hunt towers.
/dmz/operators#intel-investor: Slightly increases the cash you extract.
/dmz/operators#intel-hostile-looter: Hostiles sometimes drop an Uncommon printer ingredient, with a small chance of a Rare one.
/dmz/operators#intel-container-looter: Chance to find an extra item in containers.
/dmz/operators#intel-thermal-padding: Hides you from UAVs and downgrades enemy Advanced UAVs to standard UAV detection.
/dmz/operators#intel-uav-upgrade: Increases UAV range and duration and turns UAVs into Advanced UAVs.
/dmz/operators#intel-overwatch: UAV Towers you activate never expire.
/dmz/operators#intel-field-crafting: Craft items from Common printer resources while deployed.
/dmz/operators#intel-ai-drop-rare-loot: Named in Xbox Wire's Scout list; effect not described.
/dmz/operators#intel-metabolism: Regenerates health lost from using the tourniquet.
/dmz/operators#intel-die-hard: In Last Stand, automatically calls an exfil when you near one and gives unlimited bleed-out time.
/dmz/operators#intel-air-superiority: Captured UAV Towers and SAM Sites stay active longer.
/dmz/operators#intel-consumable-duration: Extends how long consumable effects last.
/dmz/operators#intel-impact-smokes: Releases smoke when you are downed.
/dmz/operators#intel-numb-the-pain: Applies Painkiller and Smelling Salts effects when you are revived.
/dmz/operators#intel-free-revive: Your first wound repairs itself automatically.
/dmz/operators#intel-free-tourniquet: Named in Xbox Wire's list of Survivalist traits. Its effect has not been described officially yet.
/dmz/operators#intel-minor-traits-are-ra: Minor traits, and the traits gained from operator prestige, are reportedly assigned at random, so you cannot fully choose a build. A player who made two operators saw different small trait nodes on each.
/dmz/operators#intel-extra-ammo-from-ene: One of the first traits on the left side of the trait tree makes killed enemies drop extra ammo. A player said it fixed the ammo shortage others complained about, since AI drops little ammo and ammo boxes cannot be crafted at the start.
/dmz/operators#intel-popcorn-lethals: Warfighter Minor trait: hostiles you hit with Lethals are more likely to drop Lethals.
/dmz/operators#intel-pack-rat: Scout Minor trait that raises your maximum 3D Printer resource capacity by 20%; it stacks with Resource Hoarder.
/dmz/operators#intel-deep-breath: Survivalist Minor trait that lets you hold your breath longer underwater.
/dmz/operators#intel-combat-scavenger: Minor trait: killed hostiles have a small chance to drop a printer ingredient or a valuable.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-bounty-lea: A physical FOB station listing the Top 50 Most Wanted Operators and the Top 50 Bounty Hunters, viewable globally or among friends. The Most Wanted list refreshes weekly.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-boss-board: Station for buying intel on Lieutenants with DMZ Cash and reading free information about Commanders. Extracting Lieutenant Dog Tag Cases and killing Commanders progresses the board.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-vendor: Sells weapons and other gear for DMZ Cash; bought weapons go straight to your Stash and can be modified like any other. Stock is limited and rotates, and higher DMZ levels plus printer upgrades widen the selection.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-gunsmith: Builds and customizes weapons for DMZ using DMZ Cash: buy attachments for weapons you extracted, or buy new base weapons once you have extracted their Weapon Manual. Cosmetics cost nothing to apply.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-dog-tag-ca: Trophy station that displays Dog Tags you extracted from rival Operators, with options to favorite ones you want to keep. Its storage is limited and can be expanded with 3D Printer upgrades.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-events-sta: Shows active Modern Warfare 4 events, with their challenges and limited-time unlocks.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-the-fob: The FOB is a walkable third-person hub between deployments. It starts with a handful of stations and expands to over a dozen as you level and complete Orders.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-deploy-sta: Always available. Walk through the razor-wire gate to the heavy-lift transport and choose Story Missions, Dynamic Operations or Free Roam plus an infil method.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-operators-: Pick, recover, dismiss and prestige operators and spend Trait Points.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-stash-and-: Stores extracted gear and builds the loadout for the next deployment. Shared by all Active Duty operators; starts with 40 item and 12 weapon slots.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-dmz-orders: Orders Tablet where you review and track Order chapters.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-firing-ran: Test weapons and optics against targets out past 100 m, with barricades and stance/mount testing.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-survival-k: Opens themed loot packs earned from levels, Orders and events; contents go to the Stash.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-dmz-progre: Shows the 1-70 DMZ level track and its rewards.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-3d-printer: Crafts gear from Resources and Ingredients, prints to your operator or Stash, tracks recipes and builds FOB upgrades.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-fob-upgrad: Permanent FOB upgrades are printed at the 3D Printer, each needing several prints. They raise stash and bank capacity, cut MIA recovery costs and allow rarer ingredient printing; valuables can be spent on them.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-station-up: Some DMZ levels unlock new crafting/equipment categories as station upgrades: Tacticals at 4, Lethals at 7, Field Upgrades at 12 and Fire Support at 28.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-fob-statio: A FOB guide lists the 3D Printer at DMZ level 2, the Vendor at 5, the Gunsmith at 10 and the Dog Tag Case at 20; a player also reports the Dog Tag Case opening at level 20.
/dmz/intel/field-manual#intel-no-hajin-m: There is no way to view the Hajin map from the FOB to plan routes or choose keys, and players want one added. They also can't hand stash items to squadmates at the FOB.
/dmz/printer#intel-how-crafting-works: Crafting needs a Recipe plus Resources and/or 3D Printer Ingredients. Recipes unlock through DMZ levels, DMZ Orders, or by looting and extracting with them; you can craft several copies at once and send results to the Stash or straight to your Operator.
/dmz/printer#intel-resources: Four basic Resources (Synthetics, Electronics, Chemicals, Metals) that looted items break down into automatically. They sit in a backpack pouch, show as totals in the Stash and printer menus, and take no Stash slots.
/dmz/printer#intel-3d-printer-ingredient: Specific items found in particular map areas that stay intact in your Backpack and must be extracted. Upgraded printers can also craft some Ingredients.
/dmz/printer#intel-bandage-recipe: Level 2 recipe for a consumable that restores max health for a while when you are wounded.
/dmz/printer#intel-medkit-recipe: Level 2 recipe for a consumable that repairs wounds to full health and lets you use the tourniquet to get up from Last Stand.
/dmz/printer#intel-1-plate-armor-vest-re: Level 2 recipe for a plate carrier that holds one armor plate.
/dmz/printer#intel-2-plate-armor-vest-re: Level 2 recipe for a tougher plate carrier that holds two armor plates.
/dmz/printer#intel-small-backpack-recipe: Level 2 recipe for a backpack with extra item slots.
/dmz/printer#intel-medium-backpack-recip: Level 2 recipe for a larger backpack that adds Secure Slots, which keep items safe if you fail to exfil.
/dmz/printer#intel-recipes-unlocked-by-d: The DMZ level track awards Recipes at set levels, starting with the 3D Printer basics at Level 2.
/dmz/printer#intel-crafting-categories: Printer recipes are grouped into Upgrades, Consumables, Plate Carriers, Backpacks, Tacticals, Lethals, Field Upgrades, Fire Support, Gear and Ingredients, plus a Tracked list. The June overview also mentions a Special Items group.
/dmz/printer#intel-extracting-recipes-an: Recipes and Weapon Manuals are always consumed when you extract, unlocking them permanently, and each also pays 5,000 DMZ Cash.
/dmz/printer#intel-energy-drink-recipe: Infinite stamina for a time. Recipe cost: 10 Chemicals + 10 Metals.
/dmz/printer#intel-door-breacher-charge-: Breaching consumable. Recipe cost: 1 Experimental Compounds, 5 Stock Rod and 3 Volatile Explosives.
/dmz/printer#intel-armor-box-recipe: Field upgrade that supplies extra armor plates. Recipe cost: 30 Metals and 3 Reactive Metals.
/dmz/printer#intel-disposable-parachute-: Rare parachute with three uses. Recipe cost: 30 Chemicals and 3 Rigid Synthetics.
/dmz/printer#intel-bomb-glider-recipe: Handheld explosive glider (a multiplayer killstreak). Recipe cost: 30 Chemicals, 2 Stock Rod and 5 Control Unit.
/dmz/printer#intel-recon-drone-recipe: Recipe awarded by the Counterfeit 1/2 Orders page. A Recon Drone costs 30 Metals and 3 Electronic Sensors.
/dmz/printer#intel-legendary-parachute-r: A reusable Legendary parachute. Its recipe has to be found in Hajin and extracted to unlock it; printing one then costs 2 Turned Components, 5 Nylon Cloth and 10 Rigid Synthetics. Like other gear it is lost on a failed exfil.
/dmz/printer#intel-flash-recipe: Reward from the Human Intel 1/2 Orders page. One Flash grenade prints for 10 Synthetics and 10 Chemicals; the next page's Blindness order needs four.
/dmz/printer#intel-ddos-recipe: Reward from the Underground 1/2 page. The DDOS field upgrade briefly shuts down electronics and enemy sensors nearby; it is needed for Dead Battery.
/dmz/printer#intel-decoy-grenade-recipe: Reward from the Underground 1/2 page; a Decoy Grenade prints for 10 Synthetics and 10 Chemicals and is needed for Death from Above.
/dmz/printer#intel-night-vision-goggles-: Reward from the Underground 1/2 page. Rare NVGs print for 50 Metals, 3 Printed Circuit Boards and 10 Control Units. Weak NVGs can also be picked up at a tent outside NuriGO Mall during Shopping Hacks.
/dmz/printer#intel-defibrillator-recipe: Unlocked by completing Operation Critical Extraction, the only recipe tied to a story mission. The Defibrillator instantly revives downed operators.
/dmz/printer#intel-throwing-knife-recipe: Uncommon lethal that prints for 25 Chemicals and 25 Metals once the Lethals category opens at DMZ level 7; Work Quietly asks you to print one.
/dmz/printer#intel-gas-mask-recipe: The Rare Gas Mask prints for 30 Chemicals and 3 Rigid Synthetics from DMZ level 26.
/dmz/printer#intel-tempered-armor-vest-r: Ultra plate carrier recipe found in game, not on the level track. One route: kill The Doctor at Mirae General Hospital, use his key on his Command Office and open the LT crate, then extract the recipe.
/dmz/printer#intel-large-backpack-recipe: Legendary backpack with a weapon slot and two secure slots. Its recipe prints for 2 Nylon Laminate, 5 Structural Alloy and 10 Rigid Synthetics.
/dmz/printer#intel-self-revive-kit-recip: Legendary consumable that revives you when downed, printable from DMZ level 48.
/dmz/printer#intel-comms-module: A scarce printer ingredient. Players farm Cheonwang Peak Array and the nearby tech complex and facade buildings, but often find none or just one, and are asking for higher spawn rates. Several guide videos cover farming routes.
/dmz/printer#intel-high-tenacity-fibers: The game points to the Chang-san Air Base armory and the Songdo Wharf rooftop, but players usually get just one per run on the rooftop and find the air base too hard solo; one found only three in 16 hours.
/dmz/printer#intel-electronic-sensors: The in-game hint points to commercial areas, which confuses new players; a guide video shows a spot to farm them.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-armor-plates: Your armor slot is always empty in the menu and fills with plates automatically on infil. The only ways to bring extra plates are Traits that expand the slot or the Armor Box field upgrade; plates can also be found in Hajin and at Ammo & Armor Caches.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-lieutenant-dog-t: Every slain Lieutenant drops a Dog Tag Case that all Operators can see on the Tac-Map. Picking it up broadcasts your position, and extracting with it (even one stolen from another player) progresses your Boss Board.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-basic-pack: The default backpack when no other pack is equipped, with eight slots.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-large-backpack: A bigger backpack awarded as an Epic item at DMZ Level 34.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-weapon-backpacks: Backpacks with an extra weapon slot so you can carry or extract more than two guns, or drop a built weapon for a squadmate. A Medium Weapon Backpack is an Epic reward at DMZ Level 61.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-3-plate-armor-ve: A plate carrier awarded as an Epic item at DMZ Level 37.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-2-plate-helmet-a: An Epic armor vest awarded at DMZ Level 63.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-sedative-inhaler: A consumable whose Recipe unlocks at DMZ Level 3; the blogs do not describe its effect.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-painkillers: A consumable that gives temporary health while wounded; included in Triage Kits.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-radiation-blocke: A consumable that protects against radiation; included in the Basic Triage Kit.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-smelling-salts: A consumable named in the Numb the Pain trait, which applies its effect on revive.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-self-revive-kit: Has its own Loadout slot and lets you revive yourself; Recipe unlocks at DMZ Level 48.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-defibrillator: An Uncommon consumable awarded at DMZ Level 67.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-door-breacher-ch: An Ultra-rarity consumable awarded at DMZ Level 62, used to breach doors.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-gas-mask: Headgear against gas and radiation; Recipe unlocks at DMZ Level 26. Required for the irradiated reactor area.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-durable-gas-mask: An Epic gas mask awarded at DMZ Level 68.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-night-vision-gog: Headgear that can be printed and is recommended in unpowered interiors like the casino and the underground mall.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-parachutes: Parachutes have their own Loadout slot. The Disposable Parachute recipe unlocks at Level 55 and a Legendary Parachute is awarded at Level 69; Fire Stations stock them.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-valuables: Loot marked with a gem icon that can be sold for DMZ Cash right away or spent on FOB upgrades at the 3D Printer.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-operator-rescue-: An item found in the Vault Edition Deployment Kit and the Advanced SERE Kit; the blogs do not describe how it works.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-gas-can: Operator-carried fuel cans that can be refilled at Gas Stations and Marine Gas Stations.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-snapshot-grenade: Tactical; Recipe at DMZ Level 9 and included in Recon Equipment Kits.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-throwing-knife: Lethal; Recipe at DMZ Level 7. Recommended for silent kills in high-threat areas.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-ammo-box: Field Upgrade; Recipe at DMZ Level 12. Field Upgrades do not recharge in DMZ.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-spotter-scope: Field Upgrade; Recipe at DMZ Level 12.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-armor-box: Field Upgrade; Recipe at DMZ Level 14. One of the few ways to bring extra plates into a deployment.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-inflatable-decoy: Field Upgrade; Recipe at DMZ Level 52.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-revive-pistol: Field Upgrade awarded at DMZ Level 64.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-uav-fire-support: Killstreak awarded as an Epic item at Levels 13 and 65; its Recipe unlocks at Level 31.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-care-package-fir: Killstreak whose Recipe unlocks at Level 28 with Fire Support printing; a Rare one is awarded at Level 58.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-combat-drone-fir: Epic Fire Support awarded at DMZ Level 59.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-crossfire-fire-s: A first-person A-10 airstrike Killstreak, awarded at DMZ Level 66.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-basic-armor-kit: A Uncommon Survival Kit from the DMZ level track (Level 6, 21) containing 2-Plate Carriers and an Armor Box.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-restock-kit: A Uncommon Survival Kit from the DMZ level track (Level 8, 24) containing Medium Backpacks, a Munitions Box and an Armor Box.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-basic-triage-kit: A Uncommon Survival Kit from the DMZ level track (Level 11) containing Bandages, a Med Kit, Painkillers and Radiation Blockers.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-explosives-equip: A Uncommon Survival Kit from the DMZ level track (Level 16) containing Frag Grenades, Sticky Grenades, C4, Proximity Mines and a Gun Store Weapons Locker Key.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-recon-equipment-: A Uncommon Survival Kit from the DMZ level track (Level 19, 46) containing Seeker Drone, Recon Drone, Heartbeat Sensors, Snapshot Grenades and a key (Police Station Key at 19, Black Market Weapons Locker Key at 46).
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-triage-kit: A Epic Survival Kit from the DMZ level track (Level 27) containing Bandages, Med Kits, Self Revives and Painkillers.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-trap-equipment-k: A Uncommon Survival Kit from the DMZ level track (Level 42) containing Razor Wire Traps, Trip Wires, Proximity Mines, Claymores and a Gun Store Weapons Locker Key.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-advanced-sere-ki: A Legendary Survival Kit from the DMZ level track (Level 70) containing Operator Rescue Beacons, Weapon Insurance Contracts, Self Revives and Med Kits.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-vault-edition-de: A Survival Kit for Modern Warfare 4 Vault Edition owners containing two each of Weapon Insurance Contracts, Operator Rescue Beacons, Fulton Drop Markers, Medium Backpacks and 2-Plate Carriers.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-weapon-sources-i: Weapons come from the Free Loadout, your Stash, the Gunsmith (after extracting Weapon Manuals), the Vendor, enemies and Lieutenants, dead players, military containers in Police Stations and Compounds, and Blueprints.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-gunsmith-pricing: Each attachment slot and each attachment costs DMZ Cash, and every extra slot costs more than the last; strong DMZ attachments such as suppressors, drum mags, thermal and long-range optics cost the most. A base M4 runs about 5,000 DMZ Cash.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-attachment-limit: The Gunsmith caps you at five attachments plus an Apex, but weapons found in Hajin can carry up to eight attachments.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-weapon-carry-rul: You can bring two weapons (any mix of primary and secondary) plus a melee weapon into and out of a deployment, and more with a Weapon Backpack.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-weapon-condition: Scavenged weapons can have damaged optics, broken attachments, unstable parts and field repairs that change both look and handling.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-lieutenant-weapo: Lieutenants carry custom weapons with unique attachments and camos, which can drop on death (rarely) or be found in their loot room.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-blueprints-in-dm: Any owned Blueprint can be used once for free in the DMZ Gunsmith. If that copy is lost it is gone for good, but you can buy it again at a discount compared with building the same weapon.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-signature-weapon: Vault Edition owners get one-time copies of five Signature Blueprints in their DMZ inventory and a discount on re-buying them if lost. All except the knife have five attachments plus an Apex.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-launch-weapons: Modern Warfare 4 launches with 33 weapons shared by Multiplayer, DMZ and later Warzone: 24 primaries, 8 secondaries and one melee weapon.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-shared-weapon-pr: Weapon levels, attachments and camo progress are shared between Multiplayer and DMZ. Shared attachments unlock once, and a level that would repeat one becomes a Bonus Level Up; Weapon Prestige is available.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-dmz-special-camo: Camo challenges adapt to the mode, and because AI kills count in DMZ the DMZ targets are higher. Completing a challenge in any mode unlocks the camo everywhere.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-chiral-dmz-maste: The first DMZ Mastery camo, available after the Divergence camo; it requires 2,500 kills on Tier 3 or higher enemies.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-ripple-tide-dmz-: The second DMZ Mastery camo, available after Chiral; it requires extracting with two Lieutenant dog tags in one deployment, 50 times.
/dmz/intel/armory#intel-helio-dmz-master: The final DMZ Mastery camo, available after Ripple Tide; it requires 25,000 kills with Legendary weapons on a max-level Operator.
